text:
All earthmoving activities will be exposed for as short a time as possible. This can be accomplished by excavating and mining an area in stages, with progressive backfilling and reclamation as mining progresses.
Specific mitigating measures that can be taken during and after mining include the design of properly contoured spoil banks, prompt revegetation, controlled use of the disturbed surface after revegetation, properly designed and constructed coal-haul roads, construction of an internal drainage system along roads and expansive staging and processing areas, and the use of sediment detention ponds. An interior drainage system for sediment control and a sediment detention pond are presently in use at the Westmoreland mine on Tract III.
By retaining storm water, sediment basins may also be used to reduce peak flows during heavy rainstorms and other potential flood conditions. Periodic dredging of accumulated material from sediment ponds as necessary will insure the maintenance of their designed capacity. Material dredged from the ponds could be incorporated into the topsoil if suitable, or buried.
Water in the settling basins will be monitored for chemical and biological quality as well as for concentration of suspended sediment. Water will be released only when its chemical, biological, and suspended-sediment content are within established State and Federal limits, and when its quality will not degrade the natural surface waters of the area or adversely affect local ground-water resources susceptible to recharge. The water of the sediment detention pond presently in use on Tract III is monitored monthly as part of the water quality monitoring network in use at the Westmoreland Resources mine.
